A.explanation: Amplitude of the voltage must be in volts, not cm. The vertical amplitude is $3.5\text{ cm} \times 2\text{ V cm}^{-1} = 7.0\text{ V}$.

B.explanation: Period is $4.0\text{ cm} \times 0.5\text{ ms cm}^{-1} = 2.0\text{ ms}$, so $f = 1/T = 500\text{ Hz} = 0.5\text{ kHz}$.

C.explanation: One full cycle spans $4\text{ cm}$ on the x-axis, giving $T = 2.0\text{ ms}$, not $1\text{ ms}$.

D.explanation: The x-axis is time from the $0.5\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ time-base, so the $4\text{ cm}$ repeat distance is a period, not a wavelength.

hints: Count how many $1\text{ cm}$ squares span one full sine-wave repeat along the time axis between successive peaks.

Use $f = 1/T$ for the alternating voltage and check the vertical amplitude units of $2\text{ V cm}^{-1}$ versus cm.
